Context: I'm helping Marcel (Angular/Nx engineer at Accenture) revise a leadership document, /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann_Frontend_Lead_Playbook.md, about being a Frontend Lead using Claude.ai + Claude Code on a client project. Separately from that client project's repo, Marcel maintains his own personal, cross-project dotfiles repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/manndotfiles (chezmoi-managed, macOS-only). This repo has already been fully security-audited and bootstrapped on this machine — it's clean, that is NOT in question, do not re-audit it or comment on its security posture. I just need to know what's functionally inside it.

The playbook has sections (§4-5) about maintaining a persistent "account-level" Claude Code instruction baseline (a standing behavioral configuration that applies across every conversation — e.g. anti-agreeableness framing, a working-style tone of "lead with the point, flag trade-offs, challenge like a senior reviewing a PR") and about the distinction between Claude.ai Projects (shared context across conversations) vs Claude Code (which reads a repo's own rules/context files instead). The playbook asserts "you already do this" about account-level instruction discipline, but never says concretely WHERE that configuration actually lives.

Please read, read-only, and report back on:

1. The full contents of `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/manndotfiles/claude/` directory — every file in it (settings.seed.json or similar settings file, the statusline command script, any personal-level instructions/memory files, any personal Claude Code skills, any plugin/marketplace configuration). Report exact file paths and what each configures.
2. The top-level `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/manndotfiles/README.md` — what philosophy does it state for how this dotfiles repo manages Claude Code as "configured infrastructure"?
3. A one-line note on the personal-vs-work machine-profile split (check `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` and `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` briefly) — just enough to describe that this repo distinguishes personal vs work identity/config, no need to dig deep.

Purpose: I want to draw a clean, concrete line in the revised playbook between (a) Marcel's personal/global Claude Code operating setup — which travels with him across every client and every repo, configured once in manndotfiles — versus (b) a specific project's shared rules layer (like zimmermann-pwa's `.claude/` + `AGENTS.md`, which is a team contract, not personal config). Right now the playbook treats "account-level instructions" as a vague idea with no concrete anchor.

Output: a tight report (this is secondary/supporting input, keep it short) listing exact file paths and what's configured in each (settings/permissions, statusline, default effort level, plugin curation, any personal instruction or skill files), plus one paragraph describing how this personal layer is distinct in kind from a project's shared rules layer. Do not propose or make any edits.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Re-snapshot the tracked Claude skills (listed in skills.txt) into this repo.
# Only skills named in skills.txt are copied — edit that list to add/remove.
# Dereferences symlinks and excludes venvs, build junk, media, and secrets.
set -euo pipefail
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
DST="$REPO/claude/skills"
EXCLUDES=(
  --exclude='.DS_Store' --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='.git'
  --exclude='.venv' --exclude='venv' --exclude='__pycache__' --exclude='*.pyc' --exclude='*.egg-info'
  --exclude='.env' --exclude='.env.*' --exclude='*.env'
  --exclude='*credential*' --exclude='*secret*' --exclude='*.key' --exclude='*.pem'
  --exclude='*.mp4' --exclude='*.mov' --exclude='*.mp3' --exclude='*.wav' --exclude='*.mkv' --exclude='*.webm'
  --exclude='.temp-*' --exclude='*.tmp'
)
mkdir -p "$DST"
while IFS= read -r skill; do
  case "$skill" in ''|\#*) continue ;; esac
  if [ -e "$SRC/$skill" ]; then
    rsync -aL --delete "${EXCLUDES[@]}" "$SRC/$skill/" "$DST/$skill/"
    echo "synced: $skill"
  else
    echo "skip (not found in ~/.claude/skills): $skill"
  fi
done < "$REPO/claude/skills.txt"

3	My portable dev environment, managed with [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io) and tuned for an
4	**Angular multi-frontend platform** role. One repo, two machine profiles — **personal** and
5	**work** — both macOS. chezmoi templates each config, and the `install/` scripts rebuild the
6	toolchain.
7	
8	## What's inside
9	
10	| Layer | Source | Applied by |
11	|-------|--------|-----------|
12	| Shell (`.zshrc`, `.zprofile`) | `dot_zshrc`, `dot_zprofile` | chezmoi |
13	| Git (`.gitconfig`, global ignore) | `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` | chezmoi |

15	| Node + monorepo | **fnm** + Node 22/24 + **pnpm** (corepack) + **Nx** | `install/setup.sh` |
16	| macOS packages | `Brewfile` | `install/setup.sh` |
17	| Global npm packages | `install/npm-globals.txt` | `install/setup.sh` |
18	| Claude Code (CLI, plugins, skills, settings) | `claude/` | `install/claude-setup.sh` |
19	| VS Code (extensions, settings, keybindings) | `vscode/` | `install/setup.sh` |
20	
21	> **Install policy — npm-first:** anything available on npm is installed via `npm install -g`
22	> (from `install/npm-globals.txt`), since npm ships more current versions than Homebrew casks.
23	> Homebrew carries only tools with **no** npm distribution — `git`, `gh`, `fnm`, Azure CLI, `jq`,
24	> and the VS Code app. (Postman installs on the **personal** profile only.)
25	>
26	> **Re-runs self-update:** running `setup.sh` again installs what's missing **and upgrades
27	> everything already installed to the latest version** (`brew --upgrade`, `npm i -g` latest,
28	> `code --install-extension --force`, `claude plugin update`).
29	
30	## Toolchain highlights (Angular multi-frontend focus)
31	
32	- **Angular / TS:** Angular CLI, Angular Language Service, ESLint, Prettier, Tailwind CSS
33	- **Monorepo & micro-frontends:** **Nx** (CLI + Nx Console extension), **pnpm** via corepack.
34	  *Module Federation* is added per-project, not globally — use
35	  `ng add @angular-architects/module-federation` or Nx generators
36	  (`nx g @nx/angular:host` / `nx g @nx/angular:remote`).
37	- **Cloud / CI (Azure-centric):** **Azure CLI** (`az`) + the `azure-devops` CLI extension, and
38	  the **Azure Pipelines** VS Code extension
39	- **Testing:** Playwright (Claude skill + **Playwright Test** VS Code extension)
40	- **Git & review:** git, gh, **GitLens**, **EditorConfig**
41	- **API integration:** newman (both profiles); **Postman GUI on the personal profile only**
42	- **Deploy:** Vercel CLI — **personal profile only** (`machine = work` skips it)
43	- **AI assistant:** Claude Code — *see the AI-tools caveat below*

# manndotfiles

My portable dev environment, managed with [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io) and tuned for an
**Angular multi-frontend platform** role. One repo, two machine profiles — **personal** and
**work** — both macOS. chezmoi templates each config, and the `install/` scripts rebuild the
toolchain.

## What's inside

| Layer | Source | Applied by |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Shell (`.zshrc`, `.zprofile`) | `dot_zshrc`, `dot_zprofile` | chezmoi |
| Git (`.gitconfig`, global ignore) | `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` | chezmoi |
| Angular CLI config | `dot_angular-config.json` | chezmoi |
| Node + monorepo | **fnm** + Node 22/24 + **pnpm** (corepack) + **Nx** | `install/setup.sh` |
| macOS packages | `Brewfile` | `install/setup.sh` |
| Global npm packages | `install/npm-globals.txt` | `install/setup.sh` |
| Claude Code (CLI, plugins, skills, settings) | `claude/` | `install/claude-setup.sh` |
| VS Code (extensions, settings, keybindings) | `vscode/` | `install/setup.sh` |

> **Install policy — npm-first:** anything available on npm is installed via `npm install -g`
> (from `install/npm-globals.txt`), since npm ships more current versions than Homebrew casks.
> Homebrew carries only tools with **no** npm distribution — `git`, `gh`, `fnm`, Azure CLI, `jq`,
> and the VS Code app. (Postman installs on the **personal** profile only.)
>
> **Re-runs self-update:** running `setup.sh` again installs what's missing **and upgrades
> everything already installed to the latest version** (`brew --upgrade`, `npm i -g` latest,
> `code --install-extension --force`, `claude plugin update`).

## Toolchain highlights (Angular multi-frontend focus)

- **Angular / TS:** Angular CLI, Angular Language Service, ESLint, Prettier, Tailwind CSS
- **Monorepo & micro-frontends:** **Nx** (CLI + Nx Console extension), **pnpm** via corepack.
  *Module Federation* is added per-project, not globally — use
  `ng add @angular-architects/module-federation` or Nx generators
  (`nx g @nx/angular:host` / `nx g @nx/angular:remote`).
- **Cloud / CI (Azure-centric):** **Azure CLI** (`az`) + the `azure-devops` CLI extension, and
  the **Azure Pipelines** VS Code extension
- **Testing:** Playwright (Claude skill + **Playwright Test** VS Code extension)
- **Git & review:** git, gh, **GitLens**, **EditorConfig**
- **API integration:** newman (both profiles); **Postman GUI on the personal profile only**
- **Deploy:** Vercel CLI — **personal profile only** (`machine = work` skips it)
- **AI assistant:** Claude Code — *see the AI-tools caveat below*
- **Claude status line:** minimal-mono line (model · effort · dir · git branch · context bar · usage 5h/7d bars) — `claude/statusline-command.sh`, installed & wired into `settings.json` by the setup (requires `jq`)

## Bootstrap a new Mac

### Step 0 — prerequisites
Install [Homebrew](https://brew.sh), then:
```sh
brew install chezmoi git
```

### Step 1 — apply dotfiles
```sh
chezmoi init --apply navarroangelo/manndotfiles
```
chezmoi asks **machine type (personal/work)** and **git email** once, then writes the right
`.gitconfig` for this machine. (Your name and shell config are constant across machines.)

### Step 2 — install the toolchain
```sh
~/.local/share/chezmoi/install/setup.sh
```

### Step 3 — sign back in (secrets live OUTSIDE this repo)
```sh
gh auth login          # sign in to GitHub
az login               # if the engagement uses Azure
claude                 # sign in; re-auth MCP servers as prompted
```

### Or hand it to Claude Code

If Claude Code is already on the machine, start it (`claude`) and paste this — it runs the
whole bootstrap for you:

```text
Bootstrap my dev environment from my dotfiles repo `navarroangelo/manndotfiles`:
1. If `chezmoi` or `git` are missing, install them via Homebrew.
2. Ask me whether this is a "work" or "personal" machine and which git email to use.
3. Write those two answers into ~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml under a [data] table
   (creating the directory/file if needed), e.g.:
     [data]
         machine = "work"
         email = "me@example.com"
   Then run `chezmoi init --apply navarroangelo/manndotfiles` — chezmoi reads the
   pre-seeded values and skips its interactive prompts. (Don't use `--no-tty` here — it
   does not supply answers, it just makes the prompts fail.)
4. Run `install/setup.sh`.
5. When it finishes, remind me to run `gh auth login`, `az login`, and `claude`.
Preview any command that needs sudo before running it, and stop if a step fails.
```

> Why not `--no-tty`? It suppresses the prompt's TTY, it doesn't feed it an answer — chezmoi's
> `promptStringOnce` fails with `error calling promptStringOnce: EOF` if nothing is already in
> `chezmoi.toml`. Pre-seeding `[data]` is the only reliable non-interactive path (verified against
> chezmoi v2.70.5).

## 🔒 Secrets are never committed

This repo contains **zero secrets**:
- **GitHub token** — not stored or auto-exported. If a tool (e.g. an MCP server) needs `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, set it in `~/.zshrc.local` (git-ignored) per machine.
- **SSH keys** — not stored in the repo. Add any keys you need on the new machine by hand and `chmod 600` them.
- **MCP server auth** (Supabase, Notion, Figma, etc.) — re-authenticated through `claude` on first run.

`.gitignore` blocks `*.local`, `.env*`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `id_*`, etc.

## Machine-specific overrides

Per-machine extras (git-ignored, never shared between personal and work): `~/.zshrc.local`

## Daily use

```sh
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc      # edit a tracked file (opens the source template)
chezmoi apply              # apply pending changes to $HOME
chezmoi re-add             # pull local edits back into the repo
chezmoi cd && git push     # commit & push the repo
```

To update the tracked Claude skills after editing one: `claude/sync-skills-to-repo.sh`.

## Notes & caveats

- **Work profile hardening:** on `machine = work`, `setup.sh` skips personal-only tools (Vercel CLI,
  Postman). `machine = personal` gets everything.
- **Claude permission seed:** `claude/settings.seed.json` is a single static file applied identically
  on both profiles (not templated). It excludes code-egress commands (`git push`, `gh api`,
  `vercel deploy`, `commit-push-pr`) so they always prompt, on personal and work alike.
- **Apple Silicon assumption:** `install/setup.sh` and `dot_zprofile` hardcode the `/opt/homebrew`
  Homebrew prefix. Both of Marcel's Macs are M-series, so this is intentional — if that ever changes,
  the prefix needs to fall back to `/usr/local` for Intel.
- **Reproducibility vs freshness:** the npm-first + self-updating design always installs the *latest*
  versions. If an engagement requires reproducible/pinned builds, pin versions in
  `install/npm-globals.txt` (e.g. `@angular/cli@X.Y.Z`) and drop the `--upgrade` flag.
- **Containers:** Docker Desktop is intentionally **not** auto-installed — it requires a paid
  license at enterprise scale (Accenture qualifies). If you need containers, use an IT-approved
  engine (Docker via Accenture's software catalog, or Rancher Desktop / Podman).
- **AI tools:** any AI assistant that processes code (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, etc.) is governed
  by Accenture's approved-AI-tools policy. Confirm what's sanctioned before using it on client code.
  The ChatGPT and Gemini editor extensions were removed for this reason. On `machine = work`, Claude
  Code is **not auto-installed** — the setup uses the Accenture-provisioned **Enterprise** install
  (no-training tenant) and only configures plugins/skills against it; it's auto-installed on personal only.
- **Editor sync:** `install/setup.sh` seeds `vscode/settings.json` and `keybindings.json` into VS
  Code's User dir on first run only — it never overwrites a file that's already there, so later
  live edits in the app are safe. Re-sync from a live edit with `chezmoi cd`-style manual copy, or
  just rely on VS Code's built-in *Settings Sync* (via GitHub) for day-to-day drift.

329	## Custom HTTP Headers
330	
331	Configure custom headers for all HTTP requests via environment variables. Useful for:

333	- Identifying automated traffic to your backend

338

354	
355	Headers are automatically applied when using `helpers.createContext()`:

359	const page = await context.newPage();
360	// All requests from this page include your custom headers

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Claude Code: install marketplaces, plugins, personal skills, and seed settings.
# Usage: claude-setup.sh [REPO_ROOT]
set -uo pipefail
REPO="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"

if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "  ! claude CLI not found — skipping Claude setup."
  exit 0
fi

echo "  Adding plugin marketplaces..."
while IFS='=' read -r name repo; do
  case "$name" in ''|\#*) continue ;; esac
  claude plugin marketplace add "$repo" 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "    ! marketplace failed: $repo"
done < "$REPO/claude/marketplaces.txt"

echo "  Refreshing marketplaces..."
claude plugin marketplace update 2>/dev/null || true

echo "  Installing / updating plugins..."
while IFS= read -r plugin; do
  case "$plugin" in ''|\#*) continue ;; esac
  claude plugin install "$plugin" 2>/dev/null \
    || echo "    ! plugin failed: $plugin"
  claude plugin update "$plugin" 2>/dev/null || true
done < "$REPO/claude/plugins.txt"

echo "  Syncing personal skills..."
mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude/skills"
rsync -a "$REPO/claude/skills/" "$HOME/.claude/skills/"

# Seed settings ONLY on a fresh machine — never clobber a live settings.json,
# because Claude Code rewrites it at runtime as you approve permissions.
if [ ! -f "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" ]; then
  cp "$REPO/claude/settings.seed.json" "$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
  echo "  Seeded ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  echo "  ~/.claude/settings.json already exists — left untouched (compare with settings.seed.json)."
fi

# Status line — install the script and point settings.json at it (idempotent).
mkdir -p "$HOME/.claude"
cp "$REPO/claude/statusline-command.sh" "$HOME/.claude/statusline-command.sh"
chmod +x "$HOME/.claude/statusline-command.sh"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" ]; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if jq '.statusLine = {type: "command", command: "bash ~/.claude/statusline-command.sh"}' \
      "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
    mv "$tmp" "$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
    echo "  Status line configured."
  else
    rm -f "$tmp"
    echo "  ! ~/.claude/settings.json is not valid JSON — status line NOT wired. Fix or delete it, then re-run."
  fi
else
  echo "  ! jq missing — status line script copied but not wired; install jq and re-run."
fi

## manndotfiles/claude/ — file-by-file

| Path | What it configures |
|---|---|
| `claude/settings.seed.json` | Seed for `~/.claude/settings.json`. Contains: a `permissions.allow` Bash/tool allowlist (npm/ng/tsc/tailwind, git fetch/pull/add/commit/checkout/log/reset/rebase, `gh pr view/list/diff/checks`, `vercel ls/logs/project/whoami`, `brew list`, `pip3 list`, `WebSearch`) — deliberately **excludes** code-egress commands (`git push`, `gh api`, `vercel deploy`, `commit-push-pr`), so those always prompt; `enabledPlugins` — a curated list of 20 plugins from `claude-plugins-official` (frontend-design, context7, superpowers, code-review, github, feature-dev, code-simplifier, ralph-loop, typescript-lsp, commit-commands, security-guidance, claude-md-management, figma, pr-review-toolkit, claude-code-setup, agent-sdk-dev, explanatory-output-style, plugin-dev, vercel, learning-output-style); `extraKnownMarketplaces: {}`; **`effortLevel: "high"`** (the global default-effort dial); `tui: "fullscreen"`. Per `install/claude-setup.sh`, this file is only copied to `~/.claude/settings.json` on a fresh machine — it never overwrites a live settings.json, since Claude Code rewrites that file at runtime as permissions get approved. |
| `claude/statusline-command.sh` | The statusline renderer (installed to `~/.claude/statusline-command.sh`, wired into `settings.json`'s `statusLine` key via `jq`). Minimal-mono, 24-bit Catppuccin-Mocha colors. Renders: model name · **effort level** (color escalates low→max) · cwd basename · git branch + dirty marker · context-window usage bar · 5h/7d rate-limit bars · session duration · lines added/removed · non-default output style · CLI version. |
| `claude/marketplaces.txt` | Registered plugin marketplaces. Currently just a comment: `claude-plugins-official` is built-in; "third-party marketplaces removed for compliance. Add per-machine only if vetted." |
| `claude/plugins.txt` | Flat `plugin@marketplace` list, 1:1 mirror of `enabledPlugins` above; consumed by `claude-setup.sh` to run `claude plugin install`/`update` per line. |
| `claude/skills.txt` | Allowlist of "personal Claude skills to keep portable (dev/testing only)." Currently one entry: `playwright-skill`. |
| `claude/sync-skills-to-repo.sh` | One-way snapshot tool: rsyncs each skill named in `skills.txt` **from** live `~/.claude/skills/` **into** `claude/skills/` in this repo (excludes node_modules/venvs/media/secrets/creds). This is how a personal skill edited live gets captured back into version control. |
| `claude/skills/playwright-skill/` | The one vendored personal skill (SKILL.md, run.js, lib/helpers.js, package.json, README.md, API_REFERENCE.md, LICENSE). General-purpose Playwright browser automation — auto-detects local dev servers, writes throwaway test scripts to `/tmp`, screenshots/forms/login-flow/responsive testing. Generic and cross-project by design (not tied to any client's stack). |
| `install/claude-setup.sh` (orchestrator, sibling to `claude/`) | Ties the above together: adds marketplaces → installs/updates plugins from `plugins.txt` → rsyncs `claude/skills/` into `~/.claude/skills/` → seeds `settings.seed.json` into `~/.claude/settings.json` only if absent → installs and wires the statusline script via `jq`. |

**No personal CLAUDE.md, memory file, or prose "instructions" document exists anywhere in this repo** (verified via `find` for `*claude*`, `*CLAUDE.md*`, `*memory*`, `*instructions*`). Everything under `claude/` is tool **configuration** (permissions, plugin/skill curation, an effort-level dial, a statusline UI) — not standing prose text telling the model how to reason or what tone to take. If the playbook's "anti-agreeableness / lead-with-the-point / challenge-like-a-senior-reviewer" framing is meant to be "account-level," the closest concrete anchors actually present here are behavioral dials and plugin curation (e.g., `effortLevel: "high"`, and pulling in `superpowers`/`code-review`/`pr-review-toolkit` — plugins whose skills explicitly push back on rubber-stamping, e.g. `superpowers:receiving-code-review`'s "requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement") — not a literal instructions file. Worth knowing before the playbook asserts "you already do this" with a specific file citation.

## README.md philosophy (top-level)

The README frames Claude Code as **one infrastructure layer among many**, in the same table row-for-row as shell config, git config, Angular CLI config, Node/pnpm/Nx toolchain, and VS Code — "Claude Code (CLI, plugins, skills, settings) | `claude/` | `install/claude-setup.sh`." Concretely, the stated design rules are: (1) settings are seeded once, never clobbered afterward, because Claude Code owns that file at runtime; (2) the permission seed is deliberately static/untemplated and identical on both machine profiles, explicitly preserving a prompt-gate on code-egress commands "on personal and work alike"; (3) on `machine = work`, the Claude Code **binary** is intentionally left out of auto-install — Accenture's Enterprise (no-training) install is used instead, and the repo only layers plugins/skills/settings on top of it, under an explicit caveat to "confirm what's sanctioned before using it on client code"; (4) skills are versioned bidirectionally (`sync-skills-to-repo.sh` snapshots live edits back into the repo, mirroring chezmoi's own edit/apply/re-add cycle). In short: Claude Code is managed as reproducible, idempotent, self-updating personal infrastructure — not as an app with one-off settings.

## Personal vs. work split

`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompts once for a single `machine` value (`personal`/`work`, default `personal`) plus a per-machine git `email`, while `name` stays constant; `dot_gitconfig.tmpl` then templates `[user] name/email` straight from those two chezmoi values — so one repo produces one Marcel identity but a different git author email (and, per the README, different tool-install behavior — Vercel CLI/Postman/Docker and Claude-Code-auto-install are personal-only) depending on which profile answered the prompt.

## The distinction that matters for the playbook

The `manndotfiles/claude/` layer is Marcel's personal, global **operating configuration for the tool itself** — owned and authored by one person, living in `~/.claude/` outside any repo, identical across every client and every codebase he opens Claude Code in. It governs *how the tool behaves for him* (what it's allowed to run unprompted, which plugins/skills are loaded, the default effort dial, the statusline). A project's shared-rules layer (e.g., zimmermann-pwa's `.claude/` + `AGENTS.md`) is the opposite in kind: it's authored and version-controlled collectively by a team, lives inside one specific repo, is scoped only to that codebase, and encodes *domain and process knowledge* (file-protection tiers, component scaffolding conventions, Contentful sync rules, PR/release checklists) that any contributor — human or AI — working in that repo must follow, regardless of who they are. One is "how I run this tool, everywhere, forever"; the other is "what this codebase requires of anyone working in it, right now." Note for accuracy: neither layer, as inspected, contains the specific tone/anti-agreeableness prose the playbook describes — that instruction, if it exists at all, isn't committed in this repo.
